diff --git a/.tasks.toml.example b/.tasks.toml.example
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.tasks.toml.example
@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+# tasks-axi project config — copy to `.tasks.toml` in the repo that owns the backlog.
+#
+# ── THE DELIVERY SWITCH ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# `backend` is the ONE line that decides where tasks live. It ships as
+# "markdown" on purpose: everything below is prepared so flipping it to "ado"
+# is a one-word, one-line change — and that flip is a deliberate Captain step,
+# not something a setup command or a default does for you.
+#
+# Before flipping, dry-run the exact production code path without switching:
+#
+#     tasks-axi list --backend ado
+#     tasks-axi show <some-id> --backend ado --full
+#
+# `--backend` overrides this file for one command. A green read proves the org,
+# project, area, credential, and join field; meta/followup fields wait for a write.
+backend = "markdown"
+# backend = "ado"   # ← Captain-only: flip when the ADO project is provisioned
+
+[markdown]
+path = "data/backlog.md"
+archive = "data/done-archive.md"
+done_keep = 10
+
+# ── Azure DevOps backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Read whenever `backend = "ado"` (or `--backend ado` / TASKS_AXI_BACKEND=ado).
+# Present here without being active: resolving this table has no side effects.
+[ado]
+org = "contoso"
+project = "Internal"
+# Root area path new work items land in; also scopes every read (WIQL `UNDER`),
+# so tasks-axi never sees unrelated work items in the project.
+# Single quotes: an area path contains backslashes, and tasks-axi refuses
+# doubled separators from TOML or the environment rather than guessing.
+area = 'Internal\Firstmate\main'
+
+# The join key and the tasks-axi residue. All three must exist as custom fields
+# on the work item type below BEFORE the switch. id_field must be a String field
+# for WIQL equality; meta_field and followup_field must be PlainText (long-text)
+# fields because ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject
+# or truncate their payloads. A missing id_field fails the dry read; missing
+# meta_field fails an ordinary create or update, while missing followup_field
+# fails a public-followup operation. Only this work item type is managed.
+work_item_type = "Task"
+id_field = "Custom.TasksAxiId"
+meta_field = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta"
+followup_field = "Custom.TasksAxiPublicFollowup"
+
+# ADO state names per tasks-axi state; the FIRST entry is what writes use, the
+# rest are accepted on read. These defaults write Agile-process Task states;
+# Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit mappings before the switch.
+# A dry read cannot prove write states; a wrong first entry fails on the first
+# create or transition and names the rejected state.
+state_queued = "New, To Do, Proposed"
+state_in_flight = "Active, In Progress, Doing, Committed"
+state_done = "Closed, Done, Resolved, Removed"
+
+# ── Credentials (never in this file) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# First non-empty wins: TASKS_AXI_ADO_PAT, ADO_PAT, AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT,
+# AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT — otherwise an `az account get-access-token` bearer token.
+# `az login` alone is enough on a machine that already runs the other AXIs.

+++ b/AGENTS.md
@@ -1,82 +1,101 @@
-P1 ships only the markdown backend behind a `Store` seam; sqlite (P2) and remote trackers (P3) are deferred.
+Markdown is the default backend; an Azure DevOps backend ships behind the same `Store` seam. sqlite (P2) and other remote trackers (P3) are deferred.

+meta_field = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta"

+state_done = "Closed, Done, Resolved, Removed"

+#### Switching a live backlog onto ADO
+
+`backend` is the one line that decides where tasks live, and nothing flips it for you — no default, no `setup` command.
+Changing it does not migrate data: an empty ADO scope appears as an empty backlog, and existing Markdown tasks stop being visible to the CLI. Seed the ADO items and verify a known task with `tasks-axi show <id> --backend ado --full` before switching.
+Before flipping it, dry-run the exact production code path without switching:
+
+```sh
+tasks-axi list --backend ado          # reads from ADO, changes no config
+tasks-axi show <id> --backend ado --full
+```
+
+`--backend` overrides the config file for a single command, so a green read proves the org, project, area, credential, and join field; `meta_field` is exercised by an ordinary create or update, while `followup_field` is exercised only by a public-followup operation.
+See [`.tasks.toml.example`](.tasks.toml.example) for a fully prepared table with the switch left off.
+The three custom fields (`id_field`, `meta_field`, `followup_field`) must exist on the work item type **before** the switch. Configure `id_field` as a String field for WIQL equality, and configure `meta_field` and `followup_field` as PlainText (long-text) fields; ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject or truncate their payloads. A missing `id_field` fails the dry-read WIQL request, a missing `meta_field` fails an ordinary create or update, and a missing `followup_field` fails a public-followup operation. Only items of the configured `work_item_type` are managed.
+
+The default state map writes the Azure DevOps Agile-process Task states `New`, `Active`, and `Closed`. Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit state mappings before the switch; a dry read cannot prove write states, so an incorrect mapping fails on the first create or transition and names the rejected state.
+Adds targeting In flight or Done create the work item in the queued state and then apply the ordinary optimistic transition; if the transition reports an error, its outcome is unconfirmed, so retry `start` or `done` idempotently. A requested close date remains pending until a successful `done` transition consumes it. If an item is reopened and completed again entirely in ADO between tasks-axi reads, tasks-axi continues to report its previously recorded close date.
+The three tasks-axi states map 1:1 onto `System.State`, bodies are HTML-encoded in `System.Description` and decoded on read so Boards renders their text literally, dependencies are work item links, and the public-followup obligation lives in its own field with the same canonical payload the markdown backend writes.
+Parent and discovered-from links are imported only when marked as tasks-axi-owned; ordinary native ADO hierarchy links are ignored.
+ADO reads also fail closed when a public-followup work item's title, body, or links drift from its public-safe promise through an out-of-band Boards edit. Applying the same strictness to hand-edited Markdown backlogs is a separate compatibility decision.
+`AdoStore.moveTo(id, areaPath)` implements cross-queue moves as Area Path changes, but refuses to move connected tasks outside the configured area; wiring safe area-path moves into the still markdown/path-shaped CLI `mv` verb is a follow-up.
+The ADO backend has no `prune`, `render`, archive-body, or CLI move support. `rm` checks active dependents from a best-effort snapshot, but ADO has no cross-item transaction or DELETE revision precondition, so a concurrent dependency can race that check; removal is unconditional but recoverable from the recycle bin. Public-followup delivery has the same containment: blocker state is checked before the obligation's revision-guarded patch, so a concurrent blocker reopen can race delivery advancement.

tasks-axi

2 3

4 5 6 7 8

9 10 Task and backlog manager for agents — designed with [AXI](https://github.com/kunchenguid/axi) (Agent eXperience Interface). 11 12 With its default Markdown backend, tasks-axi makes a tiny structured change to a human-readable backlog at near-zero output-token cost. 13 It edits a hand-editable `backlog.md` in place with a byte-exact round-trip, so the markdown stays the source of truth while long task bodies never bloat a `list`; the optional Azure DevOps backend keeps the same CLI over ADO work items. 14 It borrows the dependency-graph and ready-query model from [beads](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads), adds structured dispatch holds, and keeps the house style from its `*-axi` siblings - token-efficient TOON output, contextual next-step suggestions, idempotent mutations, and structured errors. 15 16 ## Why 17 18 With a Markdown backlog, regenerating every mutation through the model is expensive in output tokens and risks dropped, duplicated, or reordered items. 19 tasks-axi reduces that to the length of one short command plus a compact confirmation read back as cheap input. 20 The long status line that the model used to rewrite on every status change is now a `body`. 21 Note writes are inspect-then-update: read the current body with `show --full`, then replace it deliberately with `update --body` or `update --body-file`. 22 On the Markdown backend, pass `--archive-body` with a body replacement when the superseded body should be moved to cold history in `note-archive.md`. 23 24 ## Quick Start 25 26 Install the tasks-axi skill in the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format with [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): 27 28 ```sh 29 npx skills add kunchenguid/tasks-axi --skill tasks-axi -g 30 ``` 31 32 That is the entire setup — no npm install needed. 33 The skill teaches your agent to run tasks-axi through `npx -y tasks-axi`, so the CLI comes along on demand (Node 20+ required). 34 35 Just ask for anything that touches the backlog - filing or dispatching work, completing a task, finding dispatchable or held work - and the agent loads the skill on its own when it recognizes the task. 36 37 `-g` installs the skill for all projects; drop it to install for the current project only. 38 39 ## Other Ways to Install 40 41 The skill is the recommended path, but it is not the only one. 42 43 ### Zero setup 44 45 tasks-axi is an AXI, so any capable agent can run the CLI directly with nothing installed at all. 46 Just tell your agent: 47 48 ``` 49 Execute `npx -y tasks-axi` to manage the backlog. 50 ``` 51 52 ### Session hook 53 54 Want the current backlog fed into every agent session as ambient context instead of loading on demand? 55 Install the CLI globally and opt into the hook: 56 57 ```sh 58 npm install -g tasks-axi 59 tasks-axi setup hooks 60 ``` 61 62 This installs a `SessionStart` hook for **Claude Code**, **Codex**, and **OpenCode** that surfaces the live backlog at the start of each session. 63 **Restart your agent session after running this** so the new hook takes effect. 64 65 ## Usage 66 67 Run with no arguments for a content-first dashboard of the current backlog: 68 69 ``` 70 $ tasks-axi 71 bin: ~/.local/bin/tasks-axi 72 description: Agent ergonomic task & backlog manager for the current workspace... 73 in_flight[1]{id,title,kind,repo}: 74 homemux-h7,PERSISTENT SECONDMATE - owns HomeMux end to end,secondmate,homemux 75 summary: 76 queued: 14 77 ready: 13 78 queued[10]{id,title,kind,blocked_by}: 79 firstmate-lease-adopt,adopt the durable lease,ship,treehouse-lease-t4 80 ... 81 done: 10 retained 82 help[2]: 83 - Run `tasks-axi list --state queued` for all 14 queued tasks 84 - Run `tasks-axi ready` to see only unblocked work 85 ``` 86 87 The common mutations are one short, low-token command: 88 89 ```sh 90 # add a task (the id is the caller-supplied join key; --mint generates one) 91 tasks-axi add lavish-foo-q9 "fix summary toggle" --kind ship --repo lavish-axi --priority 2 --start 92 93 # move through the workflow 94 tasks-axi start firstmate-lease-adopt 95 tasks-axi done sm-idle-handoff-q8 --pr https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/42 96 tasks-axi done fj-task-q1 --pr https://forgejo.example.com/owner/repo/pulls/39 97 tasks-axi reopen some-task 98 99 # dependencies, holds, and the ready queue 100 tasks-axi block firstmate-lease-adopt --by treehouse-lease-t4 101 tasks-axi hold firstmate-lease-adopt --reason "captain decision pending" --kind captain 102 tasks-axi unhold firstmate-lease-adopt 103 tasks-axi ready 104 tasks-axi ready --include-held 105 106 # edit the body and title: inspect current notes, then replace the body or title deliberately 107 tasks-axi show nm-release-validation --full 108 tasks-axi update nm-release-validation --body "rewritten notes" 109 tasks-axi update nm-release-validation --body-file notes.md --archive-body 110 tasks-axi update nm-release-validation --title "clearer title" 111 112 # read the full notes on demand (truncated by default) 113 tasks-axi show homemux-h7 --full 114 115 # Markdown-only maintenance 116 tasks-axi prune --keep 10 # archives the surplus, never deletes 117 tasks-axi render # normalize the markdown in place 118 tasks-axi mv hibit-cert-cleanup --to ../homemux/data/backlog.md 119 # move a linked blocker/dependent set together 120 tasks-axi mv blocker-b1 dependent-d2 --to ../homemux/data/backlog.md 121 ``` 122 123 Output is [TOON](https://toonformat.dev)-encoded and token-efficient. 124 The long task body is truncated by default — the whole point is that `list` stays cheap; use `--full` only when you need the complete notes. 125 `update --body` and `update --body-file` replace the body wholesale, so agents should inspect the current body first and write back the curated current state rather than appending a journal entry. 126 On the Markdown backend, `--archive-body` preserves the replaced body in `note-archive.md` using the same dated markdown archive block style as done pruning. 127 Every write leads with a terse `ok:` line confirming the write result, including the resulting task state when the command changes one (e.g. `ok: start lavish-share -> In flight`, `ok: done grok-harness-g7 -> Done (pr )`, `ok: render -> normalized 3`), followed by state-aware next-step hints that never suggest an action the command just performed. 128 Mutations are idempotent and report what changed (`already: true` on a no-op), so re-running one is safe. 129 Running `done` again on an already Done task can still backfill a new `--pr`, `--report`, or `--note` without changing the original close date. 130 `hold --reason ""` records an intentional pause without turning it into prose, and `unhold ` clears it. 131 The reason must be single-line text without parentheses because parentheses are reserved for canonical markdown tags. 132 Active holds are excluded from `ready`; a hold with `--until YYYY-MM-DD` becomes inactive on and after that date, so the task can surface as ready again if nothing else blocks it. 133 Use `ready --include-held` to show dispatchable ready work and a separate `held` group with the hold reason, kind, and until date. 134 Use `list --state held` or `list --fields held,hold_reason,hold_kind,hold_until` when you need to scan active hold state directly. 135 Pass `--json` to any mutation for a machine-readable result object (`{ "ok": true, "action": …, "task": { … } }` or operation-specific result fields) instead of TOON, so an agent can confirm a write deterministically without a follow-up read. 136 For `mv`, a single task returns `id`, while a multi-task move returns first-occurrence-ordered, deduplicated `ids`, plus `from` and `to`. 137 138 Run `tasks-axi --help` for the command list, or `tasks-axi --help` for per-command usage. 139 140 ## Durable public follow-ups 141 142 A promised public final is a first-class `kind=public-followup` obligation, not a worker task or a `blocked-by` edge. 143 Create and mutate it only through the dedicated namespace: 144 145 ```sh 146 tasks-axi public-followup add public-final-ab \ 147 --request-context-file request.json \ 148 --purpose promised-final \ 149 --expected-final-file expected.json \ 150 --expires-at 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z \ 151 --json 152 153 tasks-axi public-followup bind-work public-final-ab --relation-file relation.json --json 154 tasks-axi public-followup supersede-work public-final-ab --relation rel-code --successor-file successor.json --json 155 tasks-axi public-followup work-event public-final-ab --event-file event.json --json 156 tasks-axi public-followup list --work-ref secondmate:demo/work-code-q1 --json 157 tasks-axi public-followup ready --json 158 tasks-axi public-followup begin-delivery public-final-ab --payload-hash --json 159 tasks-axi public-followup record-error public-final-ab --error-file error.json --json 160 tasks-axi public-followup record-delivery public-final-ab --receipt-file receipt.json --json 161 ``` 162 163 The request context file contains the relay-issued request id, platform, opaque `ctx1` binding, bounded public-safe summary, received time, follow-up expiry, and reservation expiry. 164 The expected-final file defines its typed outcome, stable project, required deliverable names, and `all-required` or `any-required` completion policy. 165 Relation files contain a stable `relation_id`, `{home_id, task_id}` work reference, `fulfills` or `contributes` role, required flag, and generation. 166 Completion event files use schema version 1 and bind an event id, obligation id, relation id, generation, source home, work id, typed outcome, safe deliverables, bounded public-safe outcome, and a `successor` field that is null unless the outcome supersedes the relation. 167 A posted receipt file records `state=posted`, request id, platform, attempt and chunk counts, posted time, and optional retention time. 168 Its attempt count must exactly match the currently recorded delivery attempt, including late receipts that reconcile that same attempt from `unknown` or `partial`. 169 An error file records the current attempt count, a safe delivery state, validated error code, occurrence time, optional retry time, and optional chunk counts. 170 Its attempt count must exactly match the currently recorded delivery attempt, and stale or future-attempt errors fail without mutation. 171 Expected-final types permit only their matching safe deliverables: `pr_url`, `report_path`, `commit_sha`, or `error_code`. 172 Run `tasks-axi public-followup --help` for the exact file-backed command surface and state names. 173 174 Each mutation is idempotent and returns the monotonic obligation `revision`, changed fields, and complete typed payload under `--json`. 175 Duplicate accepted event ids are no-ops, while conflicting ids, stale generations, source mismatches, malformed typed data, and changed immutable intake fields fail closed. 176 One work item can relate to several obligations, and one obligation can require work from several homes. 177 These cross-home relations are separate from same-backlog dispatch dependencies. 178 Existing same-backlog `blocked-by` edges remain delivery gates for `ready` and `begin-delivery`. 179 180 `tasks-axi ready` excludes public obligations from its ordinary `ready` worker group and exposes delivery-ready obligations only in `ready_public_followups`. 181 Use `tasks-axi public-followup ready` when handling public delivery. 182 Generic `start`, `done`, `reopen`, active removal, content or kind changes, and dispatch holds cannot bypass the public-followup state machine. 183 Only `record-delivery` with a validated terminal `posted` receipt or `waive --approved-by captain` can atomically move an obligation to Done. 184 On the Markdown backend, normal Done pruning then preserves the complete typed receipt or waiver in `done-archive.md`. 185 186 The Markdown backend stores version 1 typed data in a reserved base64url canonical-JSON HTML comment immediately below the task bullet. 187 The bounded public-safe title and `(kind: public-followup)` remain visible, but callers other than tasks-axi must not parse or rewrite the reserved comment. 188 Generic title and body updates are refused because changing the immutable public promise requires a successor obligation. 189 The typed schema permits public-safe identifiers, summaries, deliverables, receipt counters, timestamps, and validated error codes. 190 It rejects unknown fields so raw request text, parent context, author or channel ids, signed URLs, and raw platform responses cannot silently enter machine-readable output. 191 192 ## The markdown backend 193 194 `backlog.md` stays the hand-editable source of truth. 195 tasks-axi parses it leniently into a model, mutates the targeted item, and re-renders **in place** with a byte-exact round-trip on a file nobody has changed — `render(parse(src)) === src`. 196 Targeted task mutations re-render only the affected task; every other line, including free-form (no-id) notes, is preserved verbatim. 197 An item's body includes every following indented or blank line, so multi-paragraph notes and indented Markdown content move intact with the task. 198 Trailing separator blanks remain with the item's raw source for byte-exact preservation without becoming part of its structured body. 199 Maintenance commands are explicit exceptions: `render` normalizes every recognized task, `prune` trims the chosen section into the archive, and `mv` writes both source and destination backlogs. 200 `mv [...] --to ` moves one or more tasks as one atomic cross-file transaction. 201 To move a dependency-connected set, include every linked blocker and active dependent in the same command, unless the other endpoint already exists in the destination backlog. 202 The command refuses a move that would strand a dependency across the two files, while preserving intra-set `blocked-by` links and their reason strings. 203 Moved tasks are re-rendered canonically, so their multi-paragraph bodies remain intact but a trailing blank separator before the next item or section is dropped. 204 205 The read-modify-write window is guarded by an advisory lockfile, an atomic write (temp file + rename), and a fresh re-read on every invocation, so a hand-edit and a CLI-edit cannot clobber each other. 206 Task state is carried by the section header, not by the bullet style: `## In flight`, `## Queued`, and `## Done` decide whether a recognized item is in flight, queued, or done. 207 In flight parses both the legacy `- **id** - ...` form and firstmate's `- [ ] id - ...` checkbox form, while normalization renders both In flight and Queued items as `- [ ] id - ...` and Done items as `- [x] id - ...`. 208 Untouched legacy lines are still preserved byte-for-byte; only mutated or explicitly normalized tasks are rewritten. 209 210 It gently formalizes the inline tags a backlog already uses as the canonical fields: 211 212 - `(repo: X)` - the repo a task belongs to 213 - `blocked-by: ` or `blocked-by: - ` - a dependency edge, optionally with preserved free-text rationale (also `parent:` / `discovered-from:`) 214 - `(since )` - when a task started; `(merged )` / `(reported )` when it closed 215 - `(kind: X)` - task kind, when not already implied by a leading `SHIP` / `SCOUT` / `DOCS-ONLY` / `PERSISTENT SECONDMATE` word 216 - `(priority: 0-4)` - optional priority, also accepted through `add` / `update --priority` 217 - `(hold: )`, `(hold-kind: captain|external|load|parked|future)`, `(hold-until: YYYY-MM-DD)` - structured dispatch holds written by `hold` 218 - PR urls, `data//report.md` paths, and other `http(s)` urls - typed links 219 220 `tasks-axi render` rewrites every id'd task into this canonical form; free-form lines are left untouched. 221 Bare dependency edges render immediately after the title, while reason-bearing dependency edges render after the parenthetical tags so the reason stays attached to the edge on the next parse. 222 Dependency reasons are preserved metadata only; readiness still keys off the blocker id. 223 Hold reasons are preserved metadata too, but active holds are a readiness gate until cleared or until their date gate expires. 224 Existing prose markers like `HELD`, `PARKED`, `DEFERRED`, `CAPTAIN-DECISION`, and `do not dispatch` stay prose until you intentionally migrate them. 225 Map them to structured holds by preserving the original prose as the reason and choosing `captain`, `parked`, `future`, `load`, or `external` only when the text supports that bucket. 226 Do not bulk-rewrite live backlogs just to chase these tags; migrate only when touching the task or when a hold migration specifically targets them. 227 `add --blocked-by` and `block --by` require the referenced task to exist, and `rm` refuses to remove a task that still blocks active work. 228 Single-task `mv` has the same protection; use multi-task `mv` to move its active dependents with it. 229 230 ## Configuration 231 232 Backend selection and the Markdown path are resolved in this order: `--backend` / `--file` flags passed after the command, then `TASKS_AXI_BACKEND` / `TASKS_AXI_FILE` env, then a project `.tasks.toml`, then `~/.tasks-axi/config.toml`, then the defaults. 233 Without an explicit Markdown path, tasks-axi uses `backlog.md` when present, then `data/backlog.md` when present, and otherwise targets `backlog.md` for future writes. 234 235 ```toml 236 # .tasks.toml in the project root 237 backend = "markdown" 238 239 [markdown] 240 path = "data/backlog.md" 241 archive = "data/done-archive.md" 242 done_keep = 10 243 ``` 244 245 `archive` is optional; when omitted, pruned tasks are appended to `done-archive.md` next to the active backlog. 246 Body replacements with `--archive-body` append superseded bodies to `note-archive.md` next to the active backlog. 247 248 ## Backends 249 250 Backends live behind a narrow `Store` interface, so the CLI layer never knows which one is active. 251 252 | Backend | Status | 253 | ---------------------- | ----------------- | 254 | markdown | shipped | 255 | ado (Azure DevOps) | shipped (phase 1) | 256 | sqlite | planned | 257 | github / jira / linear | planned | 258 259 ### Azure DevOps 260 261 ```toml 262 backend = "ado" 263 264 [ado] 265 org = "contoso" 266 project = "Internal" 267 area = 'Internal\Firstmate\main' # optional: scope + where new work items land 268 # work_item_type = "Task" 269 # id_field = "Custom.TasksAxiId" 270 # meta_field = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta" 271 # followup_field = "Custom.TasksAxiPublicFollowup" 272 # state_queued = "New, To Do" # first entry is the value tasks-axi writes 273 # state_in_flight = "Active, In Progress" 274 # state_done = "Closed, Done" 275 ``` 276 277 Note the **single quotes** on `area`: an ADO area path Public-followup delivery has the same containment: blocker state is checked before the obligation's revision-guarded patch, so a concurrent blocker reopen can race delivery advancement. 305 306 ## Development 307 308 ```sh 309 pnpm install 310 pnpm build # tsc -> dist/ 311 pnpm test # vitest 312 pnpm lint # eslint 313 pnpm run build:skill -- --check # fail if the generated skill is stale 314 ``` 315 316 The installable skill is generated from the same description and help the CLI prints, so it can never drift. 317 318 ## Contributing 319 320 Contributions are welcome. 321 Human-authored PRs targeting `main` are raised through the [`no-mistakes`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes) gate, which runs review/test/lint/CI before opening the PR. 322 See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full workflow and repo conventions. 323 324 ## License 325 326 [MIT](LICENSE) © Kun Chen 1 # tasks-axi project config — copy to `.tasks.toml` in the repo that owns the backlog. 2 # 3 # ── THE DELIVERY SWITCH ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 4 # `backend` is the ONE line that decides where tasks live. All three must exist as custom fields 37 # on the work item type below BEFORE the switch. id_field must be a String field 38 # for WIQL equality; meta_field and followup_field must be PlainText (long-text) 39 # fields because ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject 40 # or truncate their payloads. A missing id_field fails the dry read; missing 41 # meta_field fails an ordinary create or update, while missing followup_field 42 # fails a public-followup operation. Only this work item type is managed. 43 work_item_type = "Task" 44 id_field = "Custom.TasksAxiId" 45 meta_field = "Custom.TasksAxiMeta" 46 followup_field = "Custom.TasksAxiPublicFollowup" 47 48 # ADO state names per tasks-axi state; the FIRST entry is what writes use, the 49 # rest are accepted on read. These defaults write Agile-process Task states; 50 # Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit mappings before the switch. 51 # A dry read cannot prove write states; a wrong first entry fails on the first 52 # create or transition and names the rejected state. 53 state_queued = "New, To Do, Proposed" 54 state_in_flight = "Active, In Progress, Doing, Committed" 55 state_done = "Closed, Done, Resolved, Removed" 56 57 # ── Credentials (never in this file) ────────────────────────────────────────── 58 # First non-empty wins: TASKS_AXI_ADO_PAT, ADO_PAT, AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT, 59 # AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT — otherwise an `az account get-access-token` bearer token. 60 # `az login` alone is enough on a machine that already runs the other AXIs. 1 # tasks-axi — agent notes 2 3 Agent-ergonomic task/backlog CLI in the `*-axi` family, built on `axi-sdk-js` and mirroring `gh-axi`. 4 Markdown is the default backend; an Azure DevOps backend ships behind the same `Store` seam. sqlite (P2) and other remote trackers (P3) are deferred. 5 6 ## Architecture 7 8 The CLI layer never knows which backend is active — it only talks to the `Store` interface. 9 10 - `src/cli.ts` — `runAxiCli` wiring: `DESCRIPTION`, `TOP_HELP`, the verb→handler map (with aliases create/view/edit/delete/close), the optional `task` noun prefix, and the global `--backend` / `--file` flags (stripped before handlers, parsed for `resolveContext`). 11 - `src/context.ts` — `resolveTasksContext` builds the backend `Store` + `ResolvedConfig`; every command receives this `TasksContext`. 12 - `src/store.ts` - the `Store` interface and `Capabilities`. Core contract: `create/get/update/remove/list/transition/addDep/removeDep/updatePublicFollowup`. `prune`/`render` are optional and capability-gated. 13 - `src/model.ts` — the `Task` data model (report §5). 14 - `src/pr-url.ts` — `isPrUrl`, the one canonical PR-URL seam (GitHub `/pull/` on github.com, Forgejo `/pulls/` on any lowercase DNS host) shared by prose link derivation, `--pr` validation, and public-followup `pr_url`; near-misses derive as `doc` links, never `pr`. 15 - `src/derive.ts` - worker `blocked` / `ready` / active `held` and public delivery readiness are derived in the CLI from `list` + the dep graph + hold date gates, never Store methods, so every backend gets them for free. 16 - `src/backends/markdown*.ts` — the default backend. 17 - `src/backends/ado.ts` + `ado-client.ts` — the Azure DevOps backend (see below). 18 - `src/public-followup.ts` - authoritative versioned schema, strict privacy-safe validation, canonical encoding, immutable-field checks, relation/event readiness, and terminal-state invariants for `kind=public-followup`; `src/commands/public-followup.ts` owns its dedicated CLI state machine. 19 - `src/commands/*` — one file per verb group; `src/view.ts` owns the read-side TOON projection; `src/confirm.ts` owns the write-side output (the `ok:` confirmation line, the `--json` payload, and `renderMutation`, which assembles both). 20 - Shared helpers copied from the family: `args.ts`, `body.ts`, `format.ts`, `fields.ts`, `toon.ts`, `suggestions.ts`, `skill.ts`. 21 22 ## Markdown grammar invariants (the hard part — do not regress) 23 24 `src/backends/markdown-grammar.ts` is pure parse/render with no I/O; `markdown.ts` adds the lock + atomic write. 25 26 - **Byte-exact round-trip (D1).** `render(parse(src)) === src` on any file nobody has mutated. Each entry keeps its exact original `raw` lines and is emitted verbatim unless `dirty`. A mutated task is re-rendered from its structured fields; untouched entries stay byte-exact. `test/fixtures/backlog.md` exercises every grammar feature; `test/fixtures/firstmate-backlog.md` mirrors firstmate's real `data/backlog.md` shape; a skipped-in-CI test also checks the real firstmate backlog when present. 27 - **The section header carries the state, not the bullet.** `## In flight`, `## Queued`, `## Done` decide the state. In-flight is recognized as BOTH the legacy `- **id** - …` and firstmate's GitHub-style `- [ ] id - …` checkbox; queued is `- [ ] id - …`; done is `- [x] id - …`. Render is unified on firstmate's real format: in-flight and queued both normalize to `- [ ] id - …` (done to `- [x] id - …`), so a legacy `- **id**` in-flight line normalizes to `- [ ]` when re-rendered and is **never** rewritten the other way — that keeps a tasks-axi-written file readable by firstmate (which assumes `- [ ]`). Byte-exact preservation still holds for untouched lines of either form. 28 - **Free-form lines (D7)** - any line whose first token is not a clean slug id followed by the delimiter `space-hyphen-space` is preserved verbatim and never operated on by id. The id must be immediately followed by `space-hyphen-space`. This keeps annotated lines like `go-live (CAPTAIN-GATED) - …` and `PR #31 (contributor) - …` free-form (no false positives). 29 - **Trailing-tag extraction.** Canonical tags (`(repo: X)`, `(kind: X)`, `(priority: 0-4)`, `(since DATE)`, `(merged|reported|done|closed DATE)`, `(hold: REASON)`, `(hold-kind: captain|external|load|parked|future)`, `(hold-until: DATE)`, `blocked-by:/parent:/discovered-from:`) are pulled only off the **trailing** tag-region of a line and re-appended in canonical order on render. This is what makes normalization idempotent: a mid-sentence parenthetical (e.g. `report.md (reported 2026-06-22): …`) or a non-date one (`(closed w/ link)`) is left in the prose and never duplicated or relocated. Date tags require an actual `YYYY-MM-DD`. 30 - **Dependency edges carry an optional free-text reason.** firstmate writes `blocked-by: - ` (e.g. `blocked-by: fix-login-k3 - waits on the login refactor`); the id stops at the first space and the reason runs to end-of-line, captured into `Dep.reason` and preserved across a round-trip. A reason does **not** affect `blocked`/`ready` (the graph keys off the blocker id alone), but a blocked item still stays out of `ready`. **Render-order rule:** a bare edge sits right after the title (before the parentheticals), but an edge **with a reason renders last**, after all `( … )` tags — both to match firstmate's real `(repo: …) blocked-by: - ` form and so a re-parse strips the parentheticals first and the reason never swallows a trailing tag (the idempotency trap). 31 - **Links and leading-word kinds live in the prose**, not as managed tags, so they are never duplicated. `done --pr`/`--report` append the url/path to the title text; links are re-derived by scanning. `kind` comes from a `(kind:)` tag or a leading `SHIP`/`SCOUT`/`DOCS-ONLY`/`PERSISTENT SECONDMATE` word, and the tag is emitted only when the prose does not already lead with that word. 32 - **body** = the item block under a bullet: every following indented (2-space) OR blank line, up to the next item header or free-form column-0 content (column-0 `## ` section headings are split earlier). Blank separators between paragraphs and trailing blanks before the next item/section belong to the block and move with it (`mv`/`start`/`done`/etc.). Indented pseudo-headings (e.g. ` ## Intent`) are body, never section boundaries. Owned by `parseEntries` in `markdown-grammar.ts`. 33 Note writes are inspect-then-update: `show --full`, then `update --body` or `update --body-file` with a curated replacement. 34 Add `--archive-body` when the superseded body should be preserved in `note-archive.md`. 35 - **Public-followup metadata** is one reserved ` ` line immediately below a `kind=public-followup` bullet. 36 The grammar validates it strictly on every read, excludes it from the human body, and re-emits it through render, move, transition, prune, and archive. 37 Firstmate and other callers must use `tasks-axi public-followup` and `--json`, never parse or rewrite the comment. 38 Generic worker readiness and lifecycle transitions cannot dispatch, complete, reopen, remove, or change the kind of an active obligation; only a posted receipt or Captain waiver completes it. 39 - **Concurrency:** every mutation runs under `withLock` (advisory `.lock`) and fails closed with a `LOCKED` error if another process holds the lock past the bounded timeout. 40 If the lock looks stale, the error tells the user to remove `.lock` only after confirming no `tasks-axi` process is running. 41 Corruption-safety is guaranteed independently by atomic temp-file + rename writes, and a hand-edit landing between read and write is detected and refused. 42 Reads do not lock. 43 44 ## The ADO backend 45 46 `src/backends/ado.ts` maps a tasks-axi `Task` onto an ADO work item; its header comment is the authoritative field map. The shape that matters: 47 48 - **ADO owns what ADO models**, tasks-axi owns the rest: title/state/area/description/tags/dependency links are native fields, with the body HTML-encoded in `System.Description` and decoded on read so ADO renders it as plain text; the residue (priority, hold, typed links, created/closed) rides in one JSON `meta_field`. The public-followup obligation gets its own field carrying the same canonical base64url payload the markdown backend writes, so a Relay obligation reads identically on either backend. 49 - **The join key is a custom field** (`id_field`), queried through WIQL — ADO's numeric id is exposed only as `meta.ado_id`. ADO cannot enforce custom-field uniqueness, so concurrent creates of one slug can both pass the precheck; the read-side duplicate guard then fails closed and names the slug for operator cleanup. 50 - **No force-fit:** `prune`/`render` are absent (capability-gated), `--archive-body` is a structured `UNSUPPORTED`, and `remove` sends the work item to the recycle bin. An ADO state that is not in the configured state map is a `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the state — never silently coerced. 51 - **Every JSON-patch update is optimistic:** a `{op:"test", path:"/rev"}` op leads the patch, so a concurrent ADO edit fails closed instead of clobbering. ADO DELETE has no revision precondition or cross-item transaction, so the active-dependent check is a best-effort snapshot that can race a concurrent `addDep`; removal is unconditional but recoverable from the recycle bin. Public-followup delivery likewise checks blocker state before patching only the obligation revision, so a concurrent blocker reopen can race delivery advancement. 52 - **`moveTo(id, areaPath)`** is the cross-queue move (Area Path change). Cross-scope moves of connected tasks are refused. The edge check and Area Path patch are separate ADO operations, so a concurrent relation can still split the graph; `moveTo` is not reachable from the CLI yet. Wiring safe area-path moves is a follow-up. 53 - **Tests never touch a live project:** `test/backends/fake-ado.ts` is an in-memory ADO (JSON-patch + enough WIQL). Keep new store behaviour testable through that fake rather than the REST client. `AdoRestClient` itself is covered separately through its injected `fetchImpl` seam (`test/backends/ado-client.test.ts`) — no network in either. 54 - **An unauthenticated ADO REST call returns `203` + an HTML sign-in page, not a `401`.** `response.ok` is therefore true and the body is not JSON, so `AdoRestClient.request` checks that shape before parsing and reports a rejected credential. Do not move that check below the parse. 55 - **Area paths must use single backslash separators** (`area = 'A\B'`). The minimal config reader does not process escapes, so a doubled separator from TOML or `TASKS_AXI_ADO_AREA` would point every WIQL read at an area ADO does not have; active ADO config resolution refuses it instead. 56 57 ## Backend selection is a deliberate switch, never a default 58 59 `backend` (`.tasks.toml` > `~/.tasks-axi/config.toml`, overridable by `TASKS_AXI_BACKEND` and `--backend`) defaults to `markdown` and nothing in the codebase flips it — not `setup`, not a migration, not a fallback. Keep it that way: moving a live backlog onto ADO is an operator decision. 60 `--backend ado` on a read verb (`list`, `show`) is the supported dry run: it proves org/project/area, credential, WIQL, and the join field without touching config; `meta_field` is exercised by an ordinary create or update, while `followup_field` is exercised only by a public-followup operation. `.tasks.toml.example` carries a fully prepared `[ado]` table with the switch left at `markdown`. 61 62 ## Conventions 63 64 - **Ids are caller-supplied join keys (D6)** validated by `ID_RE` (slug-shaped); `add --mint [--prefix]` generates a `slug-xx` id. 65 - **prune archives, never deletes (D4)** - surplus Done tasks are appended to `markdown.archive` or default `done-archive.md`. It keeps N _recognized_ tasks; free-form Done lines are preserved and not counted. 66 - **`done` auto-prunes** to `config.doneKeep` (default 10) and archives, unless `--no-prune`. 67 - **`done` on an already-Done task** stays idempotent but backfills supplied `--pr`, `--report`, and non-duplicate `--note` metadata without replacing the original closed date. 68 - **Dependency mutations validate targets.** `add --blocked-by` and `block --by` reject missing blockers and self-blocks. Parsed dangling blockers are still treated as resolved for legacy hand-edited files. 69 - **Blocking tasks are protected.** `rm` and single-id `mv` reject a task that still blocks active dependents; unblock or complete the dependents first. 70 - **`mv` is a multi-id atomic cross-file move.** `mv [...] --to ` moves a whole connected set in one transaction (`MarkdownStore.moveManyTo` under a two-file `withLocks`): all land or none do, no intermediate on-disk state that loses a link. Intra-set `blocked-by` edges (reason strings included) survive because both endpoints travel together; `requireNoSplitDeps` refuses and names any edge whose blocker/dependent would be stranded across the two files. Single-id `mv` is just N=1 (`moveTo` delegates to `moveManyTo`), so its byte output is unchanged. Moved items are re-rendered canonically, so trailing blank separators before the next item/section are dropped (a move-then-move-back is byte-exact only when the source had no such trailing blank). 71 - **Structured holds gate readiness.** `hold --reason "" [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--kind captain|external|load|parked|future]` writes canonical hold tags; `unhold ` clears them. 72 Hold reasons are single-line tag values without parentheses because parentheses delimit managed tags. 73 Active holds keep queued tasks out of `ready`, while `ready --include-held` emits a separate `held` group. 74 `hold-until` is inactive on and after that date. 75 `list --state held` filters to active held tasks, and hold columns are available via `--fields held,hold_reason,hold_kind,hold_until`. 76 - **Hold migration mapping.** Future migration code should map prose markers to structured holds without bulk-rewriting by hand: `HELD` / `do not dispatch` / `CAPTAIN-DECISION` -> `kind: captain` unless the text points elsewhere; `PARKED` -> `kind: parked`; `DEFERRED` -> `kind: future`; load-clearing language such as `hold until ` -> `kind: load`; external dependency wording -> `kind: external`. Preserve the original prose as the hold reason unless a safer human-readable reason is explicitly supplied. 77 - Idempotent mutations exit 0 with `already: true`; errors are `AxiError` with SDK exit codes (VALIDATION_ERROR→2, else 1). 78 - **Write ops are confirmation-forward.** Every mutation (`add`/`start`/`done`/`reopen`/`update`/`rm`/`block`/`unblock`/`hold`/`unhold`/`public-followup`/`mv`/`prune`/`render`) leads with a terse `ok:` line (built in `confirm.ts`) confirming the write result. 79 Task-state mutations include the resulting state (e.g. `ok: start -> In flight`), while maintenance/removal commands confirm their own result shape (e.g. `ok: render -> normalized `, `ok: removed `). 80 Optional structured detail follows (`add`/`update` keep the full `task:` record), then state-aware hints. 81 The `ok:` line is a plain top-level TOON scalar (no `encode()` quoting) - confirmation messages are built from bounded values (ids, names, validated urls/paths, counts) so the combined output still decodes as TOON. 82 - **Hints are state-aware, never contradictory.** A command must not suggest an action it just performed. 83 `add` branches its suggestion on the resulting state (`getSuggestions({action:"add", state})`): `--start`/in-flight → suggest `done`, queued → suggest `start`, done → suggest `reopen`. 84 Idempotent paths emit the same state-aware hint as the fresh path. 85 - **`--json` is the machine-readable success signal.** Every mutation accepts `--json`, which replaces the TOON output with a single pretty-printed object `{ ok: true, action, [already], task|id|operation fields... }` (see `renderMutation` / `taskToJson`). 86 This lets an agent confirm a write deterministically without a follow-up read. 87 Errors still use structured-error output + non-zero exit (not JSON), so `exit 0` + `ok:true` = success. 88 89 ## Entry point & the `--version` fast path 90 91 `bin/tasks-axi.ts` answers a bare `-v`/`-V`/`--version` through `axi-sdk-js/fast-path` and only then `await import`s `src/cli.js`, so the heavy command graph never loads for a version query (~31ms -> ~20ms, the node floor). 92 That makes `src/version.ts` a **leaf**: it may import node builtins and nothing else - importing anything from the command graph silently destroys the speedup. `cli.ts` re-imports `VERSION` from it, so there is still one source of the version string. 93 Any argv shape other than exactly one version flag falls through to `runAxiCli`, which remains the sole owner of the general case (e.g. `list --version` is still an unknown-flag error). 94 `test/bin/version-fast-path.test.ts` guards this deterministically with an ESM loader module trace (`test/fixtures/module-trace-*.mjs`) plus a negative control; do **not** add a wall-clock timing assertion to CI - it is flaky under runner contention. 95 96 ## Build / test / ship 97 98 - `pnpm build` (tsc), `pnpm test` (vitest, `test/` mirrors `src/`), `pnpm lint` (eslint), `pnpm run build:skill -- --check` (the generated `skills/tasks-axi/SKILL.md` is built from `DESCRIPTION` + `TOP_HELP` and must not drift — CI runs the check). 99 - `skills/tasks-axi/SKILL.md` is generated — regenerate with `pnpm run build:skill` after changing the description or top-level help; never hand-edit it. 100 - This repo is no-mistakes-gated; ship through `/no-mistakes`. 101 102 ### Release & packaging (mirrors the `*-axi` siblings) 103 104 - **Published to npm as a public package** via `release-please` → `npm publish --access public --provenance` on a release commit (`.github/workflows/release-please.yml`); the captain can also `npm publish` manually. Conventional commits drive the version bump; `release-please-config.json` + `.release-please-manifest.json` own versioning and `CHANGELOG.md`. 105 - Every `pull_request` workflow (`ci.yml`, `guard-generated-files.yml`, `no-mistakes-required.yml`) uses `paths-ignore` for the release-please output set (`.release-please-manifest.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`) so release PRs create zero runs. Job-level bot `if`s stay as defense in depth. `test/release-ci-exclusions.test.ts` derives that set from `release-please-config.json` and fails if a workflow drifts; update the ignore lists when adding `extra-files` or changing `release-type`. 106 - **The tarball ships runtime JS only.** `package.json` `files` is `dist/**/*.js` (+ `skills/tasks-axi`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`), so the `.d.ts`/`.js.map` that `tsc` emits for local debugging are kept out of the package. 107 `prepack` runs `npm run build`, so `npm pack`/`npm publish` always rebuild `dist` first. 108 In a fresh clone, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` before manual pack or publish. 109 Verify with `npm pack --dry-run` (no source/test cruft; bin is `dist/bin/tasks-axi.js` with its shebang preserved by tsc). 110 - **CI is a 3-OS matrix** (ubuntu/macos/windows) running install → build → lint → test → `build:skill --check`. The `Require no-mistakes` and `Guard generated files` checks gate every PR to `main`. 111 112 ## Follow-ups (out of P1 scope) 113 114 - Migrate firstmate's own `backlog.md` onto tasks-axi (a separate firstmate-repo change). 115 - sqlite backend (P2); github/jira/linear backends (P3) — slot in behind the existing `Store` seam. 116 - Optional: count free-form Done lines toward the prune keep, or recognize compound ids (`a / b`). 117 118 ## Maintaining this file 119 120 Keep this file for knowledge useful to almost every future agent session in this project. 121 Do not repeat what the codebase already shows; point to the authoritative file or command instead. 122 Prefer rewriting or pruning existing entries over appending new ones. 123 When updating this file, preserve this bar for all agents and keep entries concise.

9 10 Task and backlog manager for agents — designed with [AXI](https://github.com/kunchenguid/axi) (Agent eXperience Interface). 11 12 With its default Markdown backend, tasks-axi makes a tiny structured change to a human-readable backlog at near-zero output-token cost. 13 It edits a hand-editable `backlog.md` in place with a byte-exact round-trip, so the markdown stays the source of truth while long task bodies never bloat a `list`; the optional Azure DevOps backend keeps the same CLI over ADO work items. 14 It borrows the dependency-graph and ready-query model from [beads](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads), adds structured dispatch holds, and keeps the house style from its `*-axi` siblings - token-efficient TOON output, contextual next-step suggestions, idempotent mutations, and structured errors. 15 16 ## Why 17 18 With a Markdown backlog, regenerating every mutation through the model is expensive in output tokens and risks dropped, duplicated, or reordered items. 19 tasks-axi reduces that to the length of one short command plus a compact confirmation read back as cheap input. 20 The long status line that the model used to rewrite on every bind-work public-final-ab --relation-file relation.json --json 154 tasks-axi public-followup supersede-work public-final-ab --relation rel-code --successor-file successor.json --json 155 tasks-axi bounded public-safe summary, received time, follow-up expiry, and reservation expiry. 164 The expected-final file defines its typed outcome, stable project, required deliverable names, and outcome, and a `successor` field that is null unless the outcome supersedes the relation. 167 A posted receipt file records `state=posted`, request id, platform, attempt and chunk counts, posted time, and optional retention time. 168 Its attempt count must exactly match the currently recorded delivery attempt, including late receipts that reconcile that same attempt from `unknown` or `partial`. 169 the currently recorded delivery attempt, and stale or future-attempt errors fail without mutation. 171 Expected-final types permit only their matching safe deliverables: `pr_url`, `report_path`, `commit_sha`, or `error_code`. 172 Run `tasks-axi public-followup --help` for the exact file-backed command surface and state names. 173 174 Each mutation is idempotent and returns the monotonic obligation `revision`, changed fields, and complete typed payload under `--json`. 175 Duplicate accepted event ids are no-ops, while conflicting ids, stale generations, source mismatches, malformed typed data, and changed immutable intake fields fail closed. 176 One work item can relate to several obligations, and one obligation can require work from several homes. 177 These cross-home relations are separate from same-backlog dispatch dependencies. 178 Existing same-backlog `blocked-by` edges remain delivery gates for `ready` and `begin-delivery`. 179 180 `tasks-axi ready` excludes public `posted` receipt or `waive --approved-by captain` can atomically move an obligation to Done. 184 On the Markdown backend, normal Done pruning then preserves the complete typed receipt or waiver in `done-archive.md`. 185 186 The Markdown backend stores version 1 typed data in a reserved base64url canonical-JSON HTML comment immediately below the task bullet. 187 The bounded public-safe title and `(kind: public-followup)` remain visible, but callers other than tasks-axi must not parse or rewrite the reserved comment. 188 Generic title and body updates are refused because changing the immutable public promise requires a successor obligation. 189 The typed schema permits public-safe identifiers, summaries, deliverables, receipt counters, timestamps, and validated error codes. 190 It rejects unknown fields so raw request text, parent context, author or channel ids, signed URLs, and raw platform responses cannot silently enter machine-readable output. 191 192 ## The markdown backend 193 194 `backlog.md` stays the hand-editable source of truth. 195 tasks-axi parses it leniently into a model, mutates the targeted item, and re-renders **in place** with a byte-exact round-trip on a file nobody has changed — `render(parse(src)) === src`. 196 Targeted task mutations re-render only the affected task; every other line, including free-form (no-id) notes, is preserved verbatim. 197 An item's body includes every following indented or blank line, so multi-paragraph notes and indented Markdown content move intact with the task. 198 Trailing separator blanks remain with the item's raw source for byte-exact preservation without becoming part of its structured body. 199 Maintenance commands are explicit exceptions: `render` normalizes every recognized task, `prune` trims the chosen section into the archive, and `mv` writes both source and destination backlogs. 200 `mv [...] --to ` moves one or more tasks as one atomic cross-file transaction. 201 To move a dependency-connected set, include every linked blocker and active dependent in the same command, unless the other endpoint already exists in the destination backlog. 202 The command refuses a move that would strand a dependency across the two files, while preserving intra-set `blocked-by` links and their reason strings. 203 Moved tasks are re-rendered canonically, so their multi-paragraph bodies remain intact but a trailing blank separator before the next item or section is dropped. 204 205 The read-modify-write window is guarded by an advisory lockfile, an atomic write (temp file + rename), and a fresh re-read on every invocation, so a hand-edit and a CLI-edit cannot clobber each other. 206 Task state is carried by the section header, not by the bullet style: `## In flight`, `## Queued`, and `## Done` decide whether a recognized item is in flight, queued, or done. 207 In flight parses both the legacy `- **id** - ...` form and firstmate's `- [ ] id - ...` checkbox form, while normalization renders both In flight and Queued items as `- [ ] id - ...` and Done items as `- [x] id - ...`. 208 Untouched legacy lines are still preserved byte-for-byte; only mutated or explicitly normalized tasks are rewritten. 209 210 It gently formalizes the inline tags a backlog already uses as the canonical fields: 211 212 - `(repo: X)` - the repo a task belongs to 213 - `blocked-by: ` or `blocked-by: - ` - a dependency edge, optionally with preserved free-text rationale (also `parent:` / `discovered-from:`) 214 - `(since )` - when a task started; `(merged )` / `(reported )` when it closed 215 - `(kind: X)` - task kind, when not already implied by a leading `SHIP` / `SCOUT` / `DOCS-ONLY` / `PERSISTENT SECONDMATE` word 216 - `(priority: 0-4)` - optional priority, also accepted through `add` / `update --priority` 217 - `(hold: )`, `(hold-kind: captain|external|load|parked|future)`, `(hold-until: YYYY-MM-DD)` - structured dispatch holds written by `hold` 218 - PR urls, `data//report.md` paths, and other `http(s)` urls - typed links 219 220 `tasks-axi render` rewrites every id'd task into this canonical form; free-form lines are left untouched. 221 Bare dependency edges render immediately after the title, while reason-bearing dependency edges render after the parenthetical tags so the reason stays attached to the edge on the next parse. 222 Dependency reasons are preserved metadata only; readiness still keys off the blocker id. 223 Hold reasons are preserved metadata too, but active holds are a readiness gate until cleared or until their date gate expires. 224 Existing prose markers like `HELD`, `PARKED`, `DEFERRED`, `CAPTAIN-DECISION`, and `do not dispatch` stay prose until you intentionally migrate them. 225 Map them to structured holds by preserving the original prose as the reason and choosing `captain`, `parked`, `future`, `load`, or `external` only when the text supports that bucket. 226 Do not bulk-rewrite live backlogs just to chase these tags; migrate only when touching the task or when a hold migration specifically targets them. 227 `add --blocked-by` and `block --by` require the referenced task to exist, and `rm` refuses to remove a task that still blocks active work. 228 Single-task `mv` has the same protection; use multi-task `mv` to move its active dependents with it. 229 230 ## Configuration 231 232 Backend selection and the Azure DevOps answers an unauthenticated REST call with `203` and an HTML sign-in page rather than a `401`, so tasks-axi detects that shape and reports it as a rejected credential. 282 283 #### Switching a live backlog onto ADO 284 285 `backend` is the one line that decides where tasks live, and nothing flips it for you — no default, no `setup` command. 286 Changing it does not migrate data: an empty ADO scope appears as an empty backlog, and existing Markdown tasks stop being visible to the CLI. Seed the ADO items and verify a known task with `tasks-axi show --backend ado --full` before switching. 287 Before flipping it, dry-run the exact production code path without switching: 288 289 ```sh 290 tasks-axi list --backend ado # reads from ADO, changes no config 291 tasks-axi show --backend ado --full 292 ``` 293 294 `--backend` overrides the config file for a single command, so a green read proves the org, project, area, credential, and join field; `meta_field` is exercised by an ordinary create or update, while `followup_field` is exercised only by a public-followup operation. 295 See [`.tasks.toml.example`](.tasks.toml.example) for a fully prepared table with the switch left off. 296 The three custom fields (`id_field`, `meta_field`, `followup_field`) must exist on the work item type **before** the switch. Configure `id_field` as a String field for WIQL equality, and configure `meta_field` and `followup_field` as PlainText (long-text) fields; ADO String fields are limited to 255 characters and can reject or truncate their payloads. A missing `id_field` fails the dry-read WIQL request, a missing `meta_field` fails an ordinary create or update, and a missing `followup_field` fails a public-followup operation. Only items of the configured `work_item_type` are managed. 297 298 The default state map writes the Azure DevOps Agile-process Task states `New`, `Active`, and `Closed`. Scrum and Basic task workflows need explicit state mappings before the switch; a dry read cannot prove write states, so an incorrect mapping fails on the first create or transition and names the rejected state. 299 Adds targeting In flight or Done create the work item in the queued state and then apply the ordinary optimistic transition; if the transition reports an error, its outcome is unconfirmed, so retry `start` or `done` idempotently. A requested close date remains pending until a successful `done` transition consumes it. If an item is reopened and completed again entirely in ADO between tasks-axi reads, tasks-axi continues to report its previously recorded close date. 300 The three tasks-axi states map 1:1 onto `System.State`, bodies are HTML-encoded in `System.Description` and decoded on read so Boards renders their text literally, dependencies are work item links, and the public-followup obligation lives in its own field with the same canonical payload the markdown backend writes. 301 Parent and discovered-from links are imported only when marked as tasks-axi-owned; ordinary native ADO hierarchy links are ignored. 302 ADO reads also fail closed when a public-followup work item's title, body, or links drift from its public-safe promise through an out-of-band Boards edit. Applying the same strictness to hand-edited Markdown backlogs is a separate compatibility decision. 303 `AdoStore.moveTo(id, areaPath)` implements cross-queue moves as Area Path changes, but refuses to move connected tasks outside the configured area; wiring safe area-path moves into the still markdown/path-shaped CLI `mv` verb is a follow-up. 304 The ADO backend has no `prune`, `render`, archive-body, or CLI move support. `rm` checks active dependents from a best-effort snapshot, but ADO has no cross-item transaction or DELETE revision precondition, so a concurrent dependency can race that check; removal is unconditional but recoverable from the recycle bin. Public-followup delivery has the same containment: blocker state is checked before the obligation's revision-guarded patch, so a concurrent blocker reopen can race delivery advancement. 305 306 ## Development 307 308 ```sh 309 pnpm install 310 pnpm build # tsc -> dist/ 311 pnpm test # vitest 312 pnpm lint # eslint 313 pnpm run build:skill -- --check # fail if the generated skill is stale 314 ``` 315 316 The installable skill is generated from the same description and help the CLI prints, so it can never drift. 317 318 ## Contributing 319 320 Contributions are welcome. 321 Human-authored PRs targeting `main` are raised through the [`no-mistakes`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes) gate, which runs review/test/lint/CI before opening the PR. 322 See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full workflow and repo conventions. 323 324 ## License 325 326 [MIT](LICENSE) © Kun Chen 1 # tasks-axi project config — copy to `.tasks.toml` in the repo that owns the backlog. 2 # 3 # ── THE DELIVERY SWITCH ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 4 # `backend` is the ONE line that decides where tasks live. Byte-exact preservation still holds for untouched lines of either form. 28 - **Free-form lines (D7)** - any line whose first token is not a clean slug id followed by the delimiter `space-hyphen-space` is preserved verbatim and never operated on by id. The id must be immediately followed by `space-hyphen-space`. This keeps annotated lines like `go-live (CAPTAIN-GATED) - …` and `PR #31 (contributor) - …` free-form (no false positives). 29 - **Trailing-tag extraction.** Canonical tags (`(repo: X)`, `(kind: X)`, `(priority: 0-4)`, `(since DATE)`, `(merged|reported|done|closed DATE)`, `(hold: REASON)`, `(hold-kind: captain|external|load|parked|future)`, `(hold-until: DATE)`, `blocked-by:/parent:/discovered-from:`) are pulled only off the **trailing** tag-region of a line and re-appended in canonical order on render. This is what makes normalization idempotent: a mid-sentence parenthetical (e.g. `report.md (reported 2026-06-22): …`) or a non-date one (`(closed w/ link)`) is left in the prose and never duplicated or relocated. Date tags require an actual `YYYY-MM-DD`. 30 - **Dependency edges carry an optional free-text reason.** firstmate writes `blocked-by: - ` (e.g. `blocked-by: fix-login-k3 - waits on the login refactor`); the id stops at the first space and the reason runs to end-of-line, captured into `Dep.reason` and preserved across a round-trip. A reason does **not** affect `blocked`/`ready` (the graph keys off the blocker id alone), but a blocked item still stays out of `ready`. **Render-order rule:** a bare edge sits right after the title (before the parentheticals), but an edge **with a reason renders last**, after all `( … )` tags — both to match firstmate's real `(repo: …) blocked-by: - ` form and so a re-parse strips the parentheticals first and the reason never swallows a trailing tag (the idempotency trap). 31 - **Links and leading-word kinds live in the prose**, not as managed tags, so they are never duplicated. `done --pr`/`--report` append the url/path to the title text; links are re-derived by scanning. `kind` comes from a `(kind:)` tag or a leading `SHIP`/`SCOUT`/`DOCS-ONLY`/`PERSISTENT SECONDMATE` word, and the tag is emitted only when the prose does not already lead with that word. 32 - **body** = the item block under a bullet: every following indented (2-space) OR blank line, up to the next item header or free-form column-0 content (column-0 `## ` section headings are split earlier). Blank separators between paragraphs and trailing blanks before the next item/section belong to the block and move with it (`mv`/`start`/`done`/etc.). Indented pseudo-headings (e.g. ` ## Intent`) are body, never section boundaries. Owned by `parseEntries` in `markdown-grammar.ts`. 33 Note writes are inspect-then-update: `show --full`, then `update --body` or `update --body-file` with a curated replacement. 34 Add `--archive-body` when the superseded body should be preserved in `note-archive.md`. 35 - **Public-followup metadata** is one reserved ` ` line immediately below a `kind=public-followup` bullet. 36 The grammar validates it strictly on every read, excludes it from the human body, and re-emits it through render, move, transition, prune, and archive. 37 Firstmate and other callers must use `tasks-axi public-followup` and `--json`, never parse or rewrite the comment. 38 Generic worker readiness and lifecycle transitions cannot dispatch, complete, reopen, remove, or change the kind of an active obligation; only a posted receipt or Captain waiver completes it. 39 - **Concurrency:** every mutation runs under `withLock` (advisory `.lock`) and fails closed with a `LOCKED` error if another process holds the lock past the bounded timeout. 40 If the lock looks stale, the error tells the user to remove `.lock` only after confirming no `tasks-axi` process is running. 41 Corruption-safety is guaranteed independently by atomic temp-file + rename writes, and a hand-edit landing between read and write is detected and refused. 42 Reads do not lock. 43 44 ## The ADO backend 45 46 `src/backends/ado.ts` maps a tasks-axi `Task` onto an ADO work item; its header comment is the authoritative field map. The shape that matters: 47 48 - **ADO owns what ADO models**, tasks-axi owns the rest: title/state/area/description/tags/dependency links are native fields, with the body HTML-encoded in `System.Description` and decoded on read so ADO renders it as plain text; the residue (priority, hold, typed links, created/closed) rides in one JSON `meta_field`. The public-followup obligation gets its own field carrying the same canonical base64url payload the markdown backend writes, so a Relay obligation reads identically on either backend. 49 - **The join key is a custom field** (`id_field`), queried through WIQL — ADO's numeric id is exposed only as `meta.ado_id`. ADO cannot enforce custom-field uniqueness, so concurrent creates of one slug can both pass the precheck; the read-side duplicate guard then fails closed and names the slug for operator cleanup. 50 - **No force-fit:** `prune`/`render` are absent (capability-gated), `--archive-body` is a structured `UNSUPPORTED`, and `remove` sends the work item to the recycle bin. An ADO state that is not in the configured state map is a `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the state — never silently coerced. 51 - **Every JSON-patch update is optimistic:** a `{op:"test", path:"/rev"}` op leads the patch, so a concurrent ADO edit fails closed instead of clobbering. ADO DELETE has no revision precondition or cross-item transaction, so the active-dependent check is a best-effort snapshot that can race a concurrent `addDep`; removal is unconditional but recoverable from the recycle bin. Public-followup delivery likewise checks blocker state before patching only the obligation revision, so a concurrent blocker reopen can race delivery advancement. 52 - **`moveTo(id, areaPath)`** is the cross-queue move (Area Path change). Cross-scope moves of connected tasks are refused. The edge check and Area Path patch are separate ADO operations, so a concurrent relation can still split the graph; `moveTo` is not reachable from the CLI yet. Wiring safe area-path moves is a follow-up. 53 - **Tests never touch a live project:** `test/backends/fake-ado.ts` is an in-memory ADO (JSON-patch + enough WIQL). Keep new store behaviour testable through that fake rather than the REST client. `AdoRestClient` itself is covered separately through its injected `fetchImpl` seam (`test/backends/ado-client.test.ts`) — no network in either. 54 - **An unauthenticated ADO REST call returns `203` + an HTML sign-in page, not a `401`.** `response.ok` is therefore true and the body is not JSON, so `AdoRestClient.request` checks that shape before parsing and reports a rejected credential. Do not move that check below the parse. 55 - **Area paths must use single backslash separators** (`area = 'A\B'`). The minimal config reader does not process escapes, so a doubled separator from TOML or `TASKS_AXI_ADO_AREA` would point every WIQL read at an area ADO does not have; active ADO config resolution refuses it instead. 56 57 ## Backend selection is a deliberate switch, never a default 58 59 `backend` (`.tasks.toml` > `~/.tasks-axi/config.toml`, overridable by `TASKS_AXI_BACKEND` and `--backend`) defaults to `markdown` and nothing in the codebase flips it — not `setup`, not a migration, not a fallback. Keep it that way: moving a live backlog onto ADO is an operator decision. 60 `--backend ado` on a read verb (`list`, `show`) is the supported dry run: it proves org/project/area, credential, WIQL, and the join field without touching config; `meta_field` is exercised by an ordinary create or update, while `followup_field` is exercised only by a public-followup operation. `.tasks.toml.example` carries a fully prepared `[ado]` table with the switch left at `markdown`. 61 62 ## Conventions 63 64 - **Ids are caller-supplied join keys (D6)** validated by `ID_RE` (slug-shaped); `add --mint [--prefix]` generates a `slug-xx` id. 65 - **prune archives, never deletes (D4)** - surplus Done tasks are appended to `markdown.archive` or default `done-archive.md`. It keeps N _recognized_ tasks; free-form Done lines are preserved and not counted. 66 - **`done` auto-prunes** to `config.doneKeep` (default 10) and archives, unless `--no-prune`. 67 - **`done` on an already-Done task** stays idempotent but backfills supplied `--pr`, `--report`, and non-duplicate `--note` metadata without replacing the original closed date. 68 - **Dependency mutations validate targets.** `add --blocked-by` and `block --by` reject missing blockers and self-blocks. Parsed dangling blockers are still treated as resolved for legacy hand-edited files. 69 - **Blocking tasks are protected.** `rm` and single-id `mv` reject a task that still blocks active dependents; unblock or complete the dependents first. 70 - **`mv` is a multi-id atomic cross-file move.** `mv [...] --to ` moves a whole connected set in one transaction (`MarkdownStore.moveManyTo` under a two-file `withLocks`): all land or none do, no intermediate on-disk state that loses a link. Intra-set `blocked-by` edges (reason strings included) survive because both endpoints travel together; `requireNoSplitDeps` refuses and names any edge whose blocker/dependent would be stranded across the two files. Single-id `mv` is just N=1 (`moveTo` delegates to `moveManyTo`), so its byte output is unchanged. Moved items are re-rendered canonically, so trailing blank separators before the next item/section are dropped (a move-then-move-back is byte-exact only when the source had no such trailing blank). 71 - **Structured holds gate readiness.** `hold --reason "" [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--kind captain|external|load|parked|future]` writes canonical hold tags; `unhold ` clears them. 72 Hold reasons are single-line tag values without parentheses because parentheses delimit managed tags. 73 Active holds keep queued tasks out of `ready`, while `ready --include-held` emits a separate `held` group. 74 `hold-until` is inactive on and after that date. 75 `list --state held` filters to active held tasks, and hold columns are available via `--fields held,hold_reason,hold_kind,hold_until`. 76 - **Hold migration mapping.** Future migration code should map prose markers to structured holds without bulk-rewriting by hand: `HELD` / `do not dispatch` / `CAPTAIN-DECISION` -> `kind: captain` unless the text points elsewhere; `PARKED` -> `kind: parked`; `DEFERRED` -> `kind: future`; load-clearing language such as `hold until ` -> `kind: load`; external dependency wording -> `kind: external`. Preserve the original prose as the hold reason unless a safer human-readable reason is explicitly supplied. 77 - Idempotent mutations exit 0 with `already: true`; errors are `AxiError` with SDK exit codes (VALIDATION_ERROR→2, else 1). 78 - **Write ops are confirmation-forward.** Every mutation (`add`/`start`/`done`/`reopen`/`update`/`rm`/`block`/`unblock`/`hold`/`unhold`/`public-followup`/`mv`/`prune`/`render`) leads with a terse `ok:` line (built in `confirm.ts`) confirming the write result. 79 Task-state mutations include the resulting state (e.g. `ok: start -> In flight`), while maintenance/removal commands confirm their own result shape (e.g. `ok: render -> normalized `, `ok: removed `). 80 Optional structured detail follows (`add`/`update` keep the full `task:` record), then state-aware hints. 81 The `ok:` line is a plain top-level TOON scalar (no `encode()` quoting) - confirmation messages are built from bounded values (ids, names, validated urls/paths, counts) so the combined output still decodes as TOON. 82 - **Hints are state-aware, never contradictory.** A command must not suggest an action it just performed. 83 `add` branches its suggestion on the resulting state (`getSuggestions({action:"add", state})`): `--start`/in-flight → suggest `done`, queued → suggest `start`, done → suggest `reopen`. 84 Idempotent paths emit the same state-aware hint as the fresh path. 85 - **`--json` is the machine-readable success signal.** Every mutation accepts `--json`, which replaces the TOON output with a single pretty-printed object `{ ok: true, action, [already], task|id|operation fields... }` (see `renderMutation` / `taskToJson`). 86 This lets an agent confirm a write deterministically without a follow-up read. 87 Errors still use structured-error output + non-zero exit (not JSON), so `exit 0` + `ok:true` = success. 88 89 ## Entry point & the `--version` fast path 90 91 `bin/tasks-axi.ts` answers a bare `-v`/`-V`/`--version` through `axi-sdk-js/fast-path` and only then `await import`s `src/cli.js`, so the heavy command graph never loads for a version query (~31ms -> ~20ms, the node floor). 92 That makes `src/version.ts` a **leaf**: it may import node builtins and nothing else - importing anything from the command graph silently destroys the speedup. `cli.ts` re-imports `VERSION` from it, so there is still one source of the version string. 93 Any argv shape other than exactly one version flag falls through to `runAxiCli`, which remains the sole owner of the general case (e.g. `list --version` is still an unknown-flag error). 94 `test/bin/version-fast-path.test.ts` guards this deterministically with an ESM loader module trace (`test/fixtures/module-trace-*.mjs`) plus a negative control; do **not** add a wall-clock timing assertion to CI - it is flaky under runner contention. 95 96 ## Build / test / ship 97 98 - `pnpm build` (tsc), `pnpm test` (vitest, `test/` mirrors `src/`), `pnpm lint` (eslint), `pnpm run build:skill -- --check` (the generated `skills/tasks-axi/SKILL.md` is built from `DESCRIPTION` + `TOP_HELP` and must not drift — CI runs the check). 99 - `skills/tasks-axi/SKILL.md` is generated — regenerate with `pnpm run build:skill` after changing the description or top-level help; never hand-edit it. 100 - This repo is no-mistakes-gated; ship through `/no-mistakes`. 101 102 ### Release & packaging (mirrors the `*-axi` siblings) 103 104 - **Published to npm as a public package** via `release-please` → `npm publish --access public --provenance` on a release commit (`.github/workflows/release-please.yml`); the captain can also `npm publish` manually. Conventional commits drive the version bump; `release-please-config.json` + `.release-please-manifest.json` own versioning and `CHANGELOG.md`. 105 - Every `pull_request` workflow (`ci.yml`, `guard-generated-files.yml`, `no-mistakes-required.yml`) uses `paths-ignore` for the release-please output set (`.release-please-manifest.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`) so release PRs create zero runs. Job-level bot `if`s stay as defense in depth. `test/release-ci-exclusions.test.ts` derives that set from `release-please-config.json` and fails if a workflow drifts; update the ignore lists when adding `extra-files` or changing `release-type`. 106 - **The tarball ships runtime JS only.** `package.json` `files` is `dist/**/*.js` (+ `skills/tasks-axi`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`), so the `.d.ts`/`.js.map` that `tsc` emits for local debugging are kept out of the package. 107 `prepack` runs `npm run build`, so `npm pack`/`npm publish` always rebuild `dist` first. 108 In a fresh clone, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` before manual pack or publish. 109 Verify with `npm pack --dry-run` (no source/test cruft; bin is `dist/bin/tasks-axi.js` with its shebang preserved by tsc). 110 - **CI is a 3-OS matrix** (ubuntu/macos/windows) running install → build → lint → test → `build:skill --check`. The `Require no-mistakes` and `Guard generated files` checks gate every PR to `main`. 111 112 ## Follow-ups (out of P1 scope) 113 114 - Migrate firstmate's own `backlog.md` onto tasks-axi (a separate firstmate-repo change). 115 - sqlite backend (P2); github/jira/linear backends (P3) — slot in behind the existing `Store` seam. 116 - Optional: count free-form Done lines toward the prune keep, or recognize compound ids (`a / b`). 117 118 ## Maintaining this file 119 120 Keep this file for knowledge useful to almost every future agent session in this project. 121 Do not repeat what the codebase already shows; point to the authoritative file or command instead. 122 Prefer rewriting or pruning existing entries over appending new ones. 123 When updating this file, preserve this bar for all agents and keep entries concise.
